text:
emma: heads-up — hitting a weird throughput cliff on 8-GPU TP runs after the kv-cache change. throughput drops ~23% for long context workloads
liam: uhh, when did this start? after the last runtime flip?
emma: yes, after the KV cache reorg that batches prefix writes. only reproduces when TP=4x2 and sequence > 4096
priya: can you paste the profiler traces?
emma: perf-bot posted flame link: https://perf.internal/redwood/1799504321/flame — main hotspot is NCCL all-reduce stalls between chunks
hao: any numbers? message sizes?
emma: before: avg allreduce msg ~128KB, overlap 60% with compute, end-to-end 36ms per step. after: avg msg ~32KB (more fragments), overlap ~18%, step 44ms
liam: so more smaller messages -> poorer comm/compute overlap. are we splitting gradients differently now?
priya: KV cache batching can change tensor packing order which affects chunking alignment. if chunk boundary misaligns we end up with many small allreduce calls
hao: NCCL ring favors fewer large messages; tree can help for many small concurrent reductions. but ring has better BW for big transfers
emma: verified with nccl-tests: run-reduce-scatter + allgather profiles show increased latency per op when msg < 64KB
priya: try forcing NCCL to tree for a test: export NCCL_ALGO=TREE; export NCCL_MIN_NRINGS=1; then re-run the TP job
liam: quick patch I tried locally: bump chunk_bytes from 64k -> 256k in chunking logic; single-step perf improved 12% but memory pressure increased a bit
emma: posted minimal repro: code snippet

```bash
# run with forced tree
export NCCL_ALGO=TREE
python -m experiments.tp_repro --gpus 8 --seq 8192 --batch 1 --chunk-bytes 65536
```

emma: profiler snippet (top NCCL ops):
```
172ms allreduce (12 ops) avg 14.3ms op for 32KB
48ms allreduce (3 ops) avg 16ms op for 256KB
```

hao: interesting — per-op latency is not linear; many small ops add scheduling overhead
priya: also check kernel selection — smaller chunks mean shorter matmul runs, which limits ability to hide comm latency. our kernel scheduler prefers fast small kernels now which hurts overlap
liam: could be a regression in our batching heuristic after the kv change — it tries to prioritize latency and therefore emits smaller micro-batches that misalign across pipeline stages
emma: action items I propose: (1) run NCCL=tree vs ring matrix of tests for msg sizes [16k,32k,64k,128k,256k] on 8gpu TP setup (2) add instrumentation to log chunk sizes emitted by chunker (3) revert kv batching for a canary job to compare
hao: I'll run the NCCL matrix tonight and post numbers
priya: I'll add chunk size debug logging to the runtime — small change, will submit PR
liam: if tree wins consistently for <64KB we can add a heuristic: if median chunk < 64KB and tp_degree > 2 then set NCCL_ALGO=tree at runtime
emma: I'd rather we change chunk alignment first — prefer fixing source of fragmentation than switching algo dynamically. but fallbacks ok
perf-bot: ci-perf job queued: perf/tp-allreduce-msgsize-matrix/1799504321 -> https://ci.redwood/perf/1799504321
emma: thanks all — let's keep thread here, post raw CSV outputs so we can attach to the perf dashboard. small messages are noisy; need aggregated percentiles (p50/p90/p99)
hao: posted results: ring vs tree, msgsize, step latency csv link https://perf.internal/redwood/1799507389/csv — initial take: tree gains ~18% at 32KB, parity at 128KB, ring better at 256KB+
priya: cool. next: simulate kv-cache packing that causes misalignment and see if increasing chunk_bytes to 128k is safe for memory
liam: opened issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/2246 with proposed heuristic and tests
emma: great. if anyone sees customer SLO regressions, flag support-case. I'll draft playbook for ops: how to detect and toggle NCCL_ALGO or chunk_bytes for emergency mitigation
hao: will follow up with raw nccl trace (nvtx) and host timeline tomorrow
priya: PR for chunk logging in review: #3456
liam: thx — ping me on the review, I'll add unit test for chunk alignment
emma: wrapping up — main takeaway: KV cache change introduced packing misalignment -> many small allreduces -> ring suffers. fixes: chunk alignment, micro-batch tweak, or algorithm fallback. prefer alignment-first. :white_check_mark:
